dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY2026: organic revenue growth confirmed at around 3% (unchanged). Adjusted EBIT margin RAISED thanks to a more favourable tariff environment than anticipated (FY26 tariff impact now expected at ~20 M€, against ~30 M€ previously guided, i.e. ~10 M€ of incremental benefit); adjusted EBIT margin in H2 expected to be relatively stable organically vs H2 2025 (smaller COGS effect than in H1). Potential tariff refund relating to 2025 (~15 M€, contingent asset recognised) treated as neutral for the year as it is potentially offset by additional volatility in logistics costs in H2 - no guidance increment on that account absent clarification at Q3.
pointsCles: Fifth consecutive quarter of organic top-line growth (H1 +2.7%, Q2 +2.5% on a tougher comp) - Campari presents itself as the only listed spirits player in that position, gaining share in 95% of its markets (Europe sell-out +2% vs sector -1%, even stronger in the on-premise); FY26 organic ~3% confirmed and adjusted EBIT margin guidance RAISED on a friendlier tariff environment (FY impact now ~EUR 20M vs ~EUR 30M; 10% US tariff paid instead of the expected 15%; ~EUR 15M potential 2025 tariff refund booked as a contingent asset but kept OUT of guidance against H2 logistics volatility).

H1 adjusted EBIT EUR 358M (23.7% margin, +8.5% organic, +130bp margin accretion: gross margin +130bp on aperitif mix, faster-than-planned COGS productivity and low tariffs; A&P front-loaded at 17.4% of sales (-50bp); SG&A +60bp accretive toward the FY 70bp target with H2 accretion expected HIGHER - ~500 headcount cut in 2025, every group hire signed off by CEO/CFO); H2 organic EBIT margin guided roughly flat y/y as the COGS phasing normalizes and logistics costs rise.

Format innovation is the structural growth lever: Aperol on Tap (>1,000 Italian outlets, ~1.5% share of premium beer in 3 months, 22,000 spritz sold in one night at San Siro), ready-to-serve in 15 seeding markets, Aperol to Go can (UK/Belgium/Austria/GTR, 3x velocity targets, 65,000 cans at BST Hyde Park) - all incremental with gross profit per serve at or above the classic 3-2-1; Sarti Rosa is the international growth machine (48% of sales outside Germany vs 4% in 2023; US launch rationed to 1-2 bottles with reorders; #1 spirits innovation launch at Sainsbury's) and Espolon is now the #2 US premium tequila (NABCA +12%, only growing top-10 brand, +70bp share).

Portfolio streamlining nearing completion (10+ brands/businesses disposed in 18 months; new disposals of rhum agricole, Cabo Wabo and Bisquit & Dubouche - margin-dilutive, cash-intensive assets sold for ~EUR 30M with negligible EBIT, hence accretive; EUR -82M write-down of assets held for sale in H1 operating adjustments, a one-off to strip out); leverage comfortable at 2.6x with H1 working-capital seasonality (recurring FCF conversion before WC 64%) normalizing in H2; Kentucky distillery expansion on track for end-2026 (~EUR 100M program); watch items: German consumer, US whiskey/Wild Turkey, South Korea integration, rising logistics costs.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
The resynchronization thesis is on track: 5th consecutive quarter of organic growth (+2.7% S1 2026, +2.5% Q2 against a harder comp), market-share gains in 95% of key markets, and adjusted EBIT margin up 130bp to 23.7%. The key event of this refresh is the RAISED margin guidance, enabled by a materially friendlier US tariff outcome (FY26 impact now ~20M vs ~30M initially - a +10M incremental benefit fed straight into omniumEBIT 2026). Organic revenue guidance unchanged at ~3%. Portfolio rationalization is near complete after 18 months.

== THESIS READ ==
- Margin raise is tariff-driven and 2026-SPECIFIC per management - applied only to 2026, with the 2027-2030 margin trajectory unchanged (cost plan +200bp cumulative to 2027 remains the mid-term driver). Watch: whether any tariff benefit recurs in the 2027 guidance.
- H2 will not repeat all H1 gross-margin gains - management explicit (benefits pulled forward, logistics costs high). Watch: H2 margin phasing.
- House of Whiskey & Rum at -6% S1 (US category, South Korea, Russell's Reserve supply) is the soft spot in an otherwise broad portfolio. Watch: supply normalization.
- Innovation is early but real: Aperol on Tap took 1.5% of Italian premium-beer share in 3 months. Watch: scaling beyond Italy.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Adjusted-EBIT base (management APM, the most usable public mechanism). Campari communicates group adjusted net profit, not a per-share figure - basis flagged non-GAAP. S1 revenue (1,511M) was DERIVED from disclosed adjusted EBIT (358M) and margin (23.7%); the official release must be cross-checked at the next refresh.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: EBIT 650M (640 + 10M tariff benefit, 2026-only), finNet ~-109M declining with deleveraging (net debt 1,958 -> 1,300M by 2030), recurrent ETR 27.9% (S1 actual, vs 27.5% at setup), shares flat at 1,200M (no active buyback, dividend priority). 2027-2030: organic ~3%/yr, margin convergence on the +200bp cost plan. Bridge reconciles published 2025 at ~0 residual. Watch: rationalization completion by end-2026; A&P phasing into H2.

== CATALYSTS ==
9M sales (Oct); FY26 results (Mar 2027); Aperol on Tap / Campari Spritz RTS scaling; portfolio rationalization completion.

ancrages.moteur: US tariff impact for FY2026 cut by management from ~30 M€ to ~20 M€ (a 10% tariff actually paid instead of the 15% anticipated over part of H1), i.e. ~10 M€ of incremental benefit on adjusted EBIT - explicitly presented by management as tied to the tariff rate ACTUALLY PAID this year (a second investigation could still make it move), not as a structural change. Applied ONLY to 2026; 2027-2030 trajectory unchanged.

Organic revenue growth confirmed at ~3% for FY2026 (guidance reiterated), driven by a 5th consecutive quarter of growth (+2,7% H1, +2,5% Q2) and market share gains in 95% of markets - trajectory judged consistent with the organic reacceleration assumption adopted at creation, no adjustment needed.

Portfolio rationalisation programme (>10 brands/businesses divested in 18 months, including Rhum Agricole and Cabo Wabo this quarter) nearing its end, completion targeted for end-2026 - 2026 scope effect already built into the guidance (-70 M€ revenue/-30 M€ EBIT, already captured in the creation model), no further change to incorporate this refresh beyond confirmation of the timetable.

Adjusted financial charges guided at ~100 M€ for FY2026 (actual H1 26 at 44 M€, average cost of net debt stable at 4,3% despite average net debt falling to 2,0 Md€ from 2,3 Md€), improved maturity profile via the 600 M€ bond issue - taken as is, a slight adjustment vs the creation assumption (~95 M€).

Actual recurring tax rate in H1 26 of 27,9% (vs 27,5% adopted at creation, based on a historical average) - updated to 27,9% for the whole projection horizon, consistent with the most recent and most reliable data available.

Cost plan cumulating +200bp of margin targeted by 2027 confirmed on track (60bp of organic SG&A benefit already delivered in H1, against a target of 70bp for the full year) - 2027-2030 adjusted EBIT margin trajectory unchanged vs the creation thesis, the 2026 tariff benefit being treated as a distinct item and not carried forward.

Extraordinary CapEx concentrated on the Kentucky distillery, completion targeted for end-2026 (~100 M€ in total); total CapEx maintained at ~8% of revenue with no normalisation expected before 2027 at the earliest - not directly modelled in adjXXX (no dedicated CapEx line in the schema) but retained as context for the deleveraging trajectory, consistent with the creation assumption.

No sign of an active buyback programme identified in the H1 26 transcript - priority reaffirmed on deleveraging and the dividend, shares outstanding held stable at ~1200 M across the whole horizon, unchanged vs the creation thesis.
